sections.changelog:
Fixed

  • **A pair of exact answers is no longer diluted with other brands.** Coverage relaxes when demanding every word leaves the shopper with too little, and "too little" was two — so a query the catalogue answers with exactly two products relaxed anyway. "realme 12 плюс акб" put its two Realme batteries on top and then added six batteries for Xiaomi, Samsung and Infinix, each of which had dropped the brand and kept the rest; on a parts catalogue the brand is not a preference, since a battery for another phone does not fit. Two is now an answer, not a shortage. Measured against a shop's log, the 120 most searched phrases: two change — that one, and a pasted product title that loses a single near miss. The threshold stays inside the band the rule was measured on.
  • **A drain tick that runs out of budget no longer leaves the bulk flag raised.** A full reindex defers the per-object index statistics and recomputes them in one pass at the end, and the flag that defers them is a static — it lives for the request, not the run. A cron tick that hands the rest of the pass to the next tick left it up, and WP-Cron runs every due hook in one process, so the catch-up pass firing after it wrote its rows and silently skipped the statistics. The drift healed itself at the next full reindex, which on a site with scheduled reindexing off is not a schedule at all. The flag is now dropped when the tick hands the run on.
  • **`wp mvweb-ss reindex` no longer kills a running pass without being asked.** It cancelled first and started second, which made its own "already running" refusal unreachable — the cancel dropped the very lock the check reads — and silently aborted the background pass a schema upgrade had just started. It now refuses, and takes `--force` for the case where stopping the old pass is what was wanted.
  • **Two drivers on one reindex no longer walk the same ground twice.** The browser adopts a pass cron started, and a second tab adopts it too; each wrote its own cursor at the end of a batch, so the slower one could push the shared cursor backwards and everything between was indexed again. The furthest cursor now wins. Per-object writes were already idempotent, so this only ever cost time.
  • **The reindex screen no longer freezes on the count it found when it opened.** A reindex can already be under way when the button is pressed — the plugin primes one itself after a schema upgrade — and the server hands that run over rather than refusing it, precisely so the tab can finish it. The browser did the opposite: it printed one snapshot of the progress and stopped, leaving the button enabled and the number motionless while the work carried on in the background through cron. The only way to see it had moved was to reload the page and press the button again. The tab now adopts the run and drives it to the end, the same as one it started itself; the browser lease it claims keeps the cron drain from double-driving.
